exports.name: CanAccess
exports.signature: CanAccess(entityType string, permissionLevel matrix.PermissionLevel, entityIDParam string) gin.HandlerFunc
exports.description:
CanAccess is a Gin middleware that enforces RBAC permissions on protected routes.
It extracts the entity ID from the URL parameters, checks if RBAC is enabled for the organization,
and validates the user's access rights. If RBAC is disabled or the user lacks permission,
the request is aborted with an appropriate HTTP status code.

Parameters:
  - entityType: Type of resource being accessed (e.g., "project", "test_cases", "test_run")
  - permissionLevel: Required permission level (e.g., matrix.Read, matrix.Write, matrix.Delete)
  - entityIDParam: Name of the URL parameter containing the entity ID (e.g., "projectID", "testCaseID")

Behavior:
  - Returns 500 if user context is not available
  - Returns 403 if RBAC is enabled and user lacks required permission
  - Passes control to next handler if RBAC is disabled or user has permission
  - Uses global.EntityAll wildcard if entityIDParam is not found in the URL

exports.name: Do
exports.description:
Do sends an API request and returns the API response. The API response is
JSON decoded and stored in the value pointed to by v, or returned as an
error if an API error has occurred. If v implements the io.Writer
interface, the raw response body will be written to v, without attempting to
first decode it.

exports.name: MakeAPIRequest
exports.signature: MakeAPIRequest(method string, url string, data []byte, creds ...string) ([]byte, error)
exports.description:
MakeAPIRequest sends an HTTP request with optional authentication and returns the response body.

Parameters:
  - method: The HTTP method to use (e.g., "GET", "POST", "PUT").
  - url: The URL for the API endpoint.
  - data: The request payload as a byte slice (optional; can be nil for methods like GET).
  - creds: Optional. If provided, the first element is treated as the username and the second as the password
    for basic authentication. If not provided, a bearer token from global configuration is used.

Returns:
- The response body as a byte slice if the request succeeds.
- An error if there is an issue with the request, the response status is not 2xx, or the response body cannot be read.

Behavior:
- Sets the "Content-Type" header to "application/json" by default.
- Uses basic authentication if credentials are provided, otherwise uses a bearer token from global configuration.
- Reads and validates the response body.
- Returns an error for non-2xx HTTP status codes along with the response body.

functions.name: rateLimitBackoff
functions.signature: rateLimitBackoff(minDuration time.Duration, maxDuration time.Duration, resp *http.Response) time.Duration
functions.description:
rateLimitBackoff provides a callback for Client.Backoff which will use the“
RateLimit-Reset header to determine the time to wait. We add some jitter
to prevent a thundering herd.

min and max are mainly used for bounding the jitter that will be added to
the reset time retrieved from the headers. But if the final wait time is
less then min, min will be used instead.

exports.name: NewConsumers
exports.description:
NewConsumers creates and returns a new consumer instance with the provided
Azure Service Bus receiver and topic name.

Parameters:
  - receiver: The Azure Service Bus receiver that will be used to consume messages
  - topic: The topic name for this consumer

Returns:
  - Consumers: An interface implementation for message consumption

exports.name: Listen
exports.description:
Listen starts listening for messages from the Azure Service Bus queue and
sends them to the provided channel. This method runs continuously until
the context is cancelled or an error occurs.

The method implements the following behavior:
  - Prevents multiple concurrent listening sessions
  - Processes messages in batches of up to 10 messages
  - Automatically completes messages after sending them to the channel
  - Handles context cancellation gracefully
  - Logs errors and message processing events

Parameters:
  - ch: A channel where received messages will be sent as byte slices

Returns:
  - error: Returns an error if the consumer is already started or if
    context cancellation occurs

Example usage:

	consumer := NewConsumers(receiver)
	msgChan := make(chan []byte, 100)
	err := consumer.Listen(msgChan)
	if err != nil {
	    log.Fatal(err)
	}

exports.name: Stop
exports.description:
Stop gracefully stops the consumer by cancelling the listening context
and closing the Azure Service Bus receiver. This method is safe to call
multiple times and will clean up resources properly.

The method performs the following cleanup:
  - Cancels the listening context to stop message processing
  - Closes the Azure Service Bus receiver connection
  - Logs any errors that occur during cleanup

Example usage:

	consumer := NewConsumers(receiver)
	// ... start listening ...
	consumer.Stop() // Gracefully stop the consumer

exports.name: NewProducer
exports.description:
NewProducer creates a new producer instance with the provided Azure Service Bus sender.
The producer takes ownership of the sender and will close it when the producer is stopped.

Parameters:
  - ctx: Context for the operation (used for logging)
  - sender: The Azure Service Bus sender that will be used to publish messages

Returns:
  - Producer: An interface implementation for message publishing

Example usage:

	sender, err := client.NewSender(queueName, nil)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer sender.Close(context.Background())

	producer := NewProducer(ctx, sender)
	defer producer.Close()

	// Create and send a message
	message := CreateMessage("Hello, World!")
	err = producer.Send(ctx, message)
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("Failed to send message: %v", err)
	}

exports.name: Send
exports.description:
Send publishes a message to the Azure Service Bus queue. The message must be
of type *azservicebus.Message, otherwise an error is returned.

The method performs the following operations:
 1. Validates that the message is of the correct type
 2. Logs the message sending operation with timestamp
 3. Sends the message using the Azure Service Bus sender
 4. Returns any error that occurs during sending

Parameters:
  - ctx: Context for controlling the send operation timeout
  - msg: The message to send (must be *azservicebus.Message)

Returns:
  - error: Returns an error if the message is invalid or cannot be sent

Thread Safety:

	This method is thread-safe and can be called concurrently from multiple goroutines.

Example usage:

	// Create a message
	message := CreateMessage("Hello, World!")

	// Send the message
	err := producer.Send(ctx, message)
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("Failed to send message: %v", err)
		return
	}

	log.Println("Message sent successfully")

exports.name: Close
exports.description:
Close gracefully closes the producer by closing the underlying Azure Service Bus
sender connection. This method should be called when the producer is no longer
needed to ensure proper resource cleanup.

The method uses a background context for the close operation, which means it
will not be cancelled by the caller's context. This ensures that the cleanup
operation completes even if the caller's context is cancelled.

Returns:
  - error: Returns an error if the sender cannot be closed properly

Thread Safety:

	This method is thread-safe and can be called multiple times safely.

Example usage:

	producer := NewProducer(ctx, sender)
	defer producer.Close() // Ensure cleanup on function exit

	// Use the producer...
	err := producer.Send(ctx, message)
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("Failed to send message: %v", err)
	}

exports.name: SendBulk
exports.description:
SendBulk publishes multiple messages to the Azure Service Bus queue in a batch.
Each message must be of type *azservicebus.Message, otherwise an error is returned.

The method performs the following operations:
 1. Validates that all messages are of the correct type
 2. Logs the bulk message sending operation with timestamp
 3. Sends all messages using the Azure Service Bus sender
 4. Returns any error that occurs during sending

Parameters:
  - ctx: Context for controlling the send operation timeout
  - messages: Array of messages to send (each must be *azservicebus.Message)

Returns:
  - error: Returns an error if any message is invalid or cannot be sent

Thread Safety:

	This method is thread-safe and can be called concurrently from multiple goroutines.

Example usage:

	// Create multiple messages
	messages := []interface{}{
		CreateMessage("Hello, World 1!"),
		CreateMessage("Hello, World 2!"),
		CreateMessage("Hello, World 3!"),
	}

	// Send the messages in bulk
	err := producer.SendBulk(ctx, messages)
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("Failed to send messages: %v", err)
		return
	}

	log.Println("Messages sent successfully")

exports.name: CreateMessage
exports.description:
CreateMessage creates a new Azure Service Bus message with the provided body.
This is a convenience function for creating messages that can be sent using
the producer.

The function creates a message with the body as a byte slice. If you need
to send structured data, you should serialize it to JSON or another format
before calling this function.

Parameters:
  - body: The message body as a string

Returns:
  - *azservicebus.Message: A new Azure Service Bus message ready to be sent

Example usage:

	// Create a simple text message
	message := CreateMessage("Hello, World!")

	// Create a JSON message
	jsonData := `{"key": "value", "timestamp": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`
	message := CreateMessage(jsonData)

	// Send the message
	err := producer.Send(ctx, message)
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("Failed to send message: %v", err)
	}

types.name: producer
types.description:
producer implements the Producer interface and manages message publishing to
Azure Service Bus queues. It provides methods to send messages and gracefully
close the producer connection.

The producer wraps an Azure Service Bus sender and provides a simplified
interface for sending messages to queues. It handles message validation,
logging, and connection management.

Key Features:
  - Message validation and type checking
  - Structured logging for message operations
  - Graceful connection cleanup
  - Context-aware operations with timeout support

exports.name: NewSubscriber
exports.description:
NewSubscriber creates a new subscriber instance and takes ownership of the provided
consumers. The subscriber will manage the lifecycle of all consumers and stop them
when the subscriber itself is stopped.

The function performs the following setup:
 1. Creates individual channels for each consumer
 2. Starts all consumers in separate goroutines
 3. Merges all consumer channels into a single message channel
 4. Starts the message processing goroutine
 5. Returns the configured subscriber instance

Parameters:
  - consumers: List of consumer instances that will provide messages
  - keyFn: Function to extract routing keys from messages of type T

Returns:
  - Subscriber[T]: A configured subscriber instance ready to accept subscriptions
  - error: Returns an error if the subscriber cannot be initialized

Example usage:

	type MyMessage struct {
		ID   string `json:"id"`
		Data string `json:"data"`
	}

	keyFn := func(msg *MyMessage) string {
		return msg.ID
	}

	subscriber, err := NewSubscriber[MyMessage](consumers, keyFn)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer subscriber.Stop(context.Background())

	// Add a subscription
	msgChan := subscriber.Add("message-123")
	defer subscriber.Remove("message-123")

	// Process messages
	for msg := range msgChan {
		fmt.Printf("Received message: %+v\n", msg)
	}

exports.name: Add
exports.description:
Add creates a new subscription for the given key and returns a channel where
messages with that key will be sent. If a subscription already exists for the
key, the existing channel is returned.

The channel is created with a buffer size of 1 to prevent the producer from
getting blocked when sending messages.

Parameters:
  - key: The unique identifier for this subscription

Returns:
  - chan *T: A channel that will receive messages of type T for this subscription

Thread Safety:

	This method is thread-safe and uses a mutex to protect the subscriptions map.

Example usage:

	msgChan := subscriber.Add("user-123")
	defer subscriber.Remove("user-123")

	// Listen for messages
	for msg := range msgChan {
		processMessage(msg)
	}

exports.name: Clear
exports.description:
Clear removes all active subscriptions and closes all associated channels.
This method is useful for cleaning up all subscriptions at once, such as
during application shutdown or when resetting the subscriber state.

Thread Safety:

	This method is thread-safe and uses a mutex to protect the subscriptions map.

Example usage:

	// Clear all subscriptions
	subscriber.Clear()

exports.name: Stop
exports.description:
Stop gracefully stops the subscriber and all its managed consumers.
This method performs a coordinated shutdown with timeout support to ensure
all resources are properly cleaned up.

The shutdown process:
 1. Stops all consumers with timeout support
 2. Waits for the message processing goroutine to complete
 3. Waits for all in-flight message processing to finish
 4. Logs the shutdown result

Parameters:
  - ctx: Context for controlling the shutdown timeout

Thread Safety:

	This method is thread-safe and can be called multiple times safely.

Example usage:

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	subscriber.Stop(ctx)

exports.name: Remove
exports.description:
Remove removes the subscription associated with the given key and closes
the corresponding channel. If no subscription exists for the key, this
method does nothing.

This method is useful for cleaning up individual subscriptions when they
are no longer needed, such as when a client disconnects or a specific
message type is no longer required.

Parameters:
  - key: The unique identifier of the subscription to remove

Thread Safety:

	This method is thread-safe and uses a read-write mutex for efficient
	access to the subscriptions map.

Example usage:

	// Remove a specific subscription
	subscriber.Remove("user-123")

types.name: subscriber
types.description:
subscriber is a generic implementation of the Subscriber interface that manages
message subscriptions and routing. It coordinates multiple consumers and routes
incoming messages to appropriate subscribers based on message keys.

Type Parameters:
  - T: The type of messages that will be subscribed to and processed

The subscriber maintains a thread-safe map of subscription keys to channels,
where each channel receives messages of type T. When a message arrives, it's
deserialized and routed to the appropriate subscriber based on the key extracted
from the message.

Key Features:
  - Thread-safe subscription management
  - Automatic message routing based on keys
  - Graceful shutdown with timeout support
  - Concurrent message processing
  - Consumer lifecycle management

functions.name: process
functions.description:
process is the main message processing loop that runs in a separate goroutine.
It continuously reads messages from the merged consumer channel, deserializes them,
and routes them to the appropriate subscribers based on the extracted key.

The processing is done concurrently for each message to improve performance.
Messages are automatically removed from the subscription map after being sent
to prevent memory leaks.

Message Flow:
 1. Read message from the merged channel
 2. Deserialize JSON message to type T
 3. Extract routing key using keyFn
 4. Find the appropriate subscriber channel
 5. Send message to subscriber (if exists)
 6. Remove subscription to prevent memory leaks
 7. Handle any errors gracefully

Thread Safety:

	This method uses a mutex to safely access the subscriptions map when
	routing messages to subscribers.

with a test plan title, optionally a description and a list of all test cases in the project. Your 
job is to suggest all the test cases that match the test plan title and description. Each test cases 
contains "Test Case Title" and other test case details. You are to return all matching test cases' 
test case IDs, each separated by "###". For example, Test plan details - {'Test plan title': 'Plan to 
test basic functionality', 'Test plan description': 'Check basic funtionality like login and logout is 
working correctly.','Test cases':[{'ID':'ALDOWKDMANDJEIFMA','Title': "Login", "Description":"Check login"},

You will now be presented with the data and you are to strictly suggest the next step after given steps in exactly the 
same format as in the example. Do not add any text before and after the test case IDs and the entire response should 
just consist of the test IDs without any additional explanation. Make sure that the IDs are separated by ### in the beginning
Do not give testcase id which do not exist in input testcases.`

functions.name: handleStaleLeasesWithLock
functions.description:
handleStaleLeasesWithLock processes stale leases using SELECT FOR UPDATE to ensure atomicity.
It handles two types of stale jobs:
1. DISPATCHED jobs with expired lease_until (LEASE_EXPIRED)
2. RUNNING jobs that have been running for more than 1 hour (RUNNING_TIMEOUT)

functions.name: handleStaleLeasesProbabilistic
functions.description:
handleStaleLeasesProbabilistic processes stale leases using a probabilistic approach
to ensure only a subset of workers handle stale leases without explicit locking

functions.name: deriveStatusFromK8sJob
removeStaleJobs
functions.description:
removeStaleJobs marks jobs as FAILED if they appear to have crashed or become stuck.
Detection logic:
- DISPATCHED/RUNNING jobs: crashed if lease_until < NOW (heartbeat stopped)

The heartbeat mechanism in test-manager-migrator updates lease_until every minute,
extending it by 5 minutes. If a pod crashes, the lease expires and we detect it here.

functions.name: markJobAsCrashed
functions.signature: (*Repository) markJobAsCrashed(ctx context.Context, jobID string, currentStatus string, errorCode string, errorMessage string) error
functions.description:
markJobAsCrashed updates a job to FAILED status with crash error details and also updates
related import_job_projects to FAILED status.

functions.name: removeStaleJobsProbabilistic
functions.description:
removeStaleJobsProbabilistic detects crashed/stale jobs and marks them as FAILED.
Detection is based on:
- DISPATCHED/RUNNING jobs: uses lease_until field (heartbeat expired = pod crashed)

functions.name: updateJobStatusWithLock
functions.signature: (*Repository) updateJobStatusWithLock(ctx context.Context, jobID string, expectedStatus string, newStatus string, errorCode string, errorMessage string) error
functions.description:
updateJobStatusWithLock atomically updates job status using SELECT FOR UPDATE and optimistic locking.
This ensures no race conditions when multiple pods try to update the same job.

functions.name: deleteStaleJobFromDB
functions.description:
deleteStaleJobFromDB deletes a job from the database that no longer has a corresponding K8s job.
This is used during reconciliation to clean up stale records for terminal state jobs.

exports.name: CreateMultipleDuplicateTestCases
exports.signature: (*Repository) CreateMultipleDuplicateTestCases(ctx context.Context, testCases map[string]models.TestCase, payload global.DecodeTransferTestCasesToFolderRequest) error
exports.description:
CreateMultipleDuplicateTestCases : This function bulk duplicates the test cases along with all their related entities

The function performs the following operations:
1. Creates new test cases with updated folder and project IDs
2. Fetches and duplicates related entities in parallel using goroutines:
  - Test steps and their configurations
  - BDD scenarios
  - Test commits with version history
  - Snapshots for test case versions
  - Test step infos with entity mappings
  - Tags and dynamic fields
  - Attachments for all entities

3. Updates all foreign key references to maintain data integrity
4. Handles special cases like entity_id mapping in test_step_infos
5. Updates latest_test_commit_id in both tests and test_cases tables

Performance optimizations:
- Uses goroutines for independent fetch operations
- Batches database operations where possible
- Uses NewRelic segments for monitoring

functions.name: computeRevertDisabled
functions.description:
computeRevertDisabled calculates whether revert should be disabled for commits
based on KaneAI version groups.
Group 1: KaneAI version 1
Group 2: KaneAI version 2 (and above)
Version 0: Unsaved commits - treated as part of the first non-zero version's group
Logic: Revert is only allowed for commits in the same group as the active version.
First mismatch → block revert for that commit and all earlier commits.

exports.name: GetNextExecutionGroup
exports.signature: (*Repository) GetNextExecutionGroup(ctx context.Context, testRunID string, cursor *int) (*models.ExecutionGroup, error)
exports.description:
GetNextExecutionGroup returns the next consecutive executable group of test run instances, ordered by serial_no.

Grouping rules:
- Instances are considered in ascending serial_no order (never by ID).
- Instances are grouped only if their derived execution keys match exactly:
  - web: (web, os) - grouped by type and OS
  - mobile and mobile-browser: (mobile-group) - grouped together when consecutive since both will run on Linux VM

- Grouping stops at the first mismatch (non-matching key).

Cursor semantics:
- cursor is the last processed serial_no (nil means start from the beginning)
- next cursor is the serial_no of the last instance in the returned group
- returns (nil, nil) when no more instances remain

Fail-fast behavior:
- if a TRI cannot be joined to tests (tests.type is NULL) => error
- for WEB tests, if env OS is missing => error

exports.name: GetFirstGroupType
exports.description:
GetFirstGroupType returns the test type of the first execution group for sequential heterogeneous runs.
Returns "web" if the first group contains web tests, "mobile" if it contains mobile/mobile-browser tests.
Returns empty string if no instances are found.
For web tests, validates that OS is configured (matching deriveExecutionKey validation).

functions.name: GetNextExecutionGroup
functions.signature: (*Repository) GetNextExecutionGroup(ctx context.Context, testRunID string, cursor *int) (*models.ExecutionGroup, error)
functions.description:
GetNextExecutionGroup returns the next consecutive executable group of test run instances, ordered by serial_no.

Grouping rules:
- Instances are considered in ascending serial_no order (never by ID).
- Instances are grouped only if their derived execution keys match exactly:
  - web: (web, os) - grouped by type and OS
  - mobile and mobile-browser: (mobile-group) - grouped together when consecutive since both will run on Linux VM

- Grouping stops at the first mismatch (non-matching key).

Cursor semantics:
- cursor is the last processed serial_no (nil means start from the beginning)
- next cursor is the serial_no of the last instance in the returned group
- returns (nil, nil) when no more instances remain

Fail-fast behavior:
- if a TRI cannot be joined to tests (tests.type is NULL) => error
- for WEB tests, if env OS is missing => error

exports.name: FetchTestRunSecretByConfigMap
exports.signature: (service) FetchTestRunSecretByConfigMap(ctx context.Context, testRunConfig map[string][]global.TestRunConfig, is_mobile bool, userAuthRes global.UserAuthRes) (map[string]string, bool, error)
exports.description:
FetchTestRunSecretByConfigMap processes test run configurations to extract secrets and determine SmartUI usage.
It downloads blob data for each unique test ID, processes the data immediately, and returns aggregated secrets and SmartUI flag.
This function optimizes memory usage by processing data as it's downloaded rather than storing large intermediate objects.

Parameters:
  - ctx: Context for the operation
  - testRunConfig: Map of test run configurations grouped by some key
  - is_mobile: Boolean flag indicating if this is for mobile tests
  - userAuthRes: User authentication details

Returns:
  - map[string]string: Aggregated secrets from all test configurations
  - bool: SmartUI flag indicating if any test uses SmartUI features
  - error: Any error that occurred during processing

exports.name: ProcessBlobForTestRun
exports.signature: (service) ProcessBlobForTestRun(executionData global.ExecutionResult, is_mobile bool, ctx context.Context, userAuthRes global.UserAuthRes, config global.TestAccountLoginConfig) (global.ExecutionDataTestRun, error)
exports.description:
ProcessBlobForTestRun processes a single blob's execution data to extract secrets and determine SmartUI usage.
It validates secrets against the user's secret map, processes TOTP configurations, and handles mobile-specific Google login secrets.
This function is called for each blob download to process the data immediately rather than storing it in memory.

Parameters:
  - executionData: The raw execution data from blob storage
  - is_mobile: Boolean flag indicating if this is for mobile tests
  - ctx: Context for the operation
  - userAuthRes: User authentication details
  - config: Google login configuration for mobile tests

Returns:
  - global.ExecutionDataTestRun: Processed result containing secrets and SmartUI flag
  - error: Any error that occurred during processing

functions.name: ProcessBlobForTestRun
functions.signature: (service) ProcessBlobForTestRun(executionData global.ExecutionResult, is_mobile bool, ctx context.Context, userAuthRes global.UserAuthRes, config global.TestAccountLoginConfig) (global.ExecutionDataTestRun, error)
functions.description:
ProcessBlobForTestRun processes a single blob's execution data to extract secrets and determine SmartUI usage.
It validates secrets against the user's secret map, processes TOTP configurations, and handles mobile-specific Google login secrets.
This function is called for each blob download to process the data immediately rather than storing it in memory.

Parameters:
  - executionData: The raw execution data from blob storage
  - is_mobile: Boolean flag indicating if this is for mobile tests
  - ctx: Context for the operation
  - userAuthRes: User authentication details
  - config: Google login configuration for mobile tests

Returns:
  - global.ExecutionDataTestRun: Processed result containing secrets and SmartUI flag
  - error: Any error that occurred during processing

functions.signature: (service) processBlobQueriesWithThrottling(ctx context.Context, uniqueTestIDs map[string]string, userAuthRes global.UserAuthRes, testConfigMap map[string]global.TestRunConfig, is_mobile bool) (global.ExecutionDataTestRun, error)
functions.description:
processBlobQueriesWithThrottling downloads and processes blob data for multiple test IDs with controlled concurrency.
It uses a semaphore to limit concurrent blob downloads to 5, processes each blob immediately upon download,
and aggregates all processed results into a single ExecutionDataTestRun containing merged secrets and SmartUI flag.
This function optimizes memory usage by processing data immediately rather than storing large intermediate objects.

Parameters:
  - ctx: Context for the operation
  - uniqueTestIDs: Map of test ID to commit ID for blob downloads
  - userAuthRes: User authentication details
  - testConfigMap: Map of test configurations for processing
  - is_mobile: Boolean flag indicating if this is for mobile tests

Returns:
  - global.ExecutionDataTestRun: Aggregated result containing merged secrets and SmartUI flag
  - error: Any error that occurred during processing

exports.name: MergeChannels
exports.description:
MergeChannels merges multiple channels of type T into a single channel.
This function is useful for combining messages from multiple sources
into a unified stream for processing.

The function creates a new buffered channel and starts a goroutine for
each input channel to forward messages to the main channel. When all
input channels are closed, the main channel is automatically closed.

Key Features:
  - Generic type support for any channel type
  - Automatic channel closure when all sources are exhausted
  - Buffered output channel to prevent blocking
  - Concurrent message forwarding from all sources

Parameters:
  - channels: A slice of channels to merge

Returns:
  - chan T: A single channel that receives messages from all input channels

Thread Safety:

	This function is thread-safe and can be called concurrently.

Example usage:

	// Create multiple channels
	ch1 := make(chan string, 10)
	ch2 := make(chan string, 10)
	ch3 := make(chan string, 10)

	// Merge them into a single channel
	mergedCh := MergeChannels([]chan string{ch1, ch2, ch3})

	// Send messages to individual channels
	go func() {
		ch1 <- "message from ch1"
		close(ch1)
	}()
	go func() {
		ch2 <- "message from ch2"
		close(ch2)
	}()
	go func() {
		ch3 <- "message from ch3"
		close(ch3)
	}()

	// Receive all messages from the merged channel
	for msg := range mergedCh {
		fmt.Println("Received:", msg)
	}

functions.name: MergeChannels
functions.description:
MergeChannels merges multiple channels of type T into a single channel.
This function is useful for combining messages from multiple sources
into a unified stream for processing.

The function creates a new buffered channel and starts a goroutine for
each input channel to forward messages to the main channel. When all
input channels are closed, the main channel is automatically closed.

Key Features:
  - Generic type support for any channel type
  - Automatic channel closure when all sources are exhausted
  - Buffered output channel to prevent blocking
  - Concurrent message forwarding from all sources

Parameters:
  - channels: A slice of channels to merge

Returns:
  - chan T: A single channel that receives messages from all input channels

Thread Safety:

	This function is thread-safe and can be called concurrently.

Example usage:

	// Create multiple channels
	ch1 := make(chan string, 10)
	ch2 := make(chan string, 10)
	ch3 := make(chan string, 10)

	// Merge them into a single channel
	mergedCh := MergeChannels([]chan string{ch1, ch2, ch3})

	// Send messages to individual channels
	go func() {
		ch1 <- "message from ch1"
		close(ch1)
	}()
	go func() {
		ch2 <- "message from ch2"
		close(ch2)
	}()
	go func() {
		ch3 <- "message from ch3"
		close(ch3)
	}()

	// Receive all messages from the merged channel
	for msg := range mergedCh {
		fmt.Println("Received:", msg)
	}

ToSQL builds the query and returns the SQL string with parameter values substituted.
This uses GORM's DryRun feature to generate the SQL query string.
The dry-run session is cached for performance.

	builder := executor.Builder().From("users").Select("id", "name").WhereEqual("status", "active")
	sql, err := executor.ToSQL(ctx, builder)
	fmt.Println("SQL:", sql)

exports.name: MergeChannels
exports.description:
MergeChannels merges multiple channels of type T into a single channel.
This function is useful for combining messages from multiple sources
into a unified stream for processing.

The function creates a new buffered channel and starts a goroutine for
each input channel to forward messages to the main channel. When all
input channels are closed, the main channel is automatically closed.

functions.name: rateLimitBackoff
functions.signature: rateLimitBackoff(min time.Duration, max time.Duration, attemptNum int, resp *http.Response) time.Duration
functions.description:
rateLimitBackoff provides a callback for Client.Backoff which will use the
RateLimit-Reset header to determine the time to wait. We add some jitter
to prevent a thundering herd.

min and max are mainly used for bounding the jitter that will be added to
the reset time retrieved from the headers. But if the final wait time is
less then min, min will be used instead.

  - Reading plan attributes from organization config (e.g., OrgPlanAttributes)
  - Dynamic field access when field names are determined at runtime

The key parameter can be either:
  - Go field name (e.g., "ApplePayPublic")
  - JSON tag name (e.g., "mobile_applepay")

Example:

	type Config struct {
	    Enabled bool `json:"is_enabled"`
	}
	val, err := ReturnKeyValueFromStruct[*Config, bool](&Config{Enabled: true}, "Enabled")
	// or
	val, err := ReturnKeyValueFromStruct[*Config, bool](&Config{Enabled: true}, "is_enabled")

	}

architecture.overview: Repository with 631 files across 210 modules. 6783 public exports, 1469 types, 3810 functions.

ai_analysis.pattern: Layered Service-Oriented Architecture with Domain-Driven Design

layers.name: Presentation Layer
layers.purpose: Handles HTTP requests, authentication, and API endpoints

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.purpose: Business logic orchestration and external service integration

layers.name: Domain Layer
layers.purpose: Core business entities and domain logic

ai_analysis.data_flow: Requests enter through HTTP layer, pass through middleware for authentication/validation, reach service layer for business orchestration, interact with domain models, and persist through infrastructure layer. Async processing handled via Kafka queues. Cross-cutting concerns provide logging, configuration, and error handling throughout.
strengths: Clear separation of concerns with distinct layers
Comprehensive testing infrastructure with multiple execution environments
Robust observability with health checks, tracing, and logging
Scalable architecture with async processing via Kafka
weaknesses: High module count (160+) indicates potential over-fragmentation
Duplicate module names suggest inconsistent organization
Complex interdependencies between layers may impact maintainability
Large monolithic structure despite modular design
Potential for tight coupling between service and domain layers
recommendations: Consolidate duplicate modules and establish clear naming conventions
Consider extracting independent services into separate microservices
Implement dependency injection to reduce tight coupling
Create module boundaries documentation to guide future development
Establish API contracts between major components to enable independent evolution
Consider implementing hexagonal architecture patterns for better testability

ai_summary.overview: Lambda Test Forge Service is a comprehensive test management system (TMS) service built in Go that provides APIs for managing test execution, automation jobs, and test data across different platforms including mobile and desktop environments. It integrates with LambdaTest's testing infrastructure to orchestrate test builds, runs, and reporting.
ai_summary.purpose: To provide a centralized backend service for managing automated and manual testing workflows, test case execution, build management, and integration with various testing platforms and third-party services like Jira
key_features: Test build creation and execution management
Integration with automation frameworks and CI/CD pipelines
Test case and test plan management
Real-time test execution monitoring and reporting
Integration with external services (Jira, Kafka, Redis)
ai_summary.architecture_style: Microservices architecture with layered design pattern (repository-service-endpoint layers)
main_components: Test Management Core (test runs, builds, cases)
suggestions: Consider breaking down the large monolithic service into smaller, more focused microservices
Implement API documentation using OpenAPI/Swagger specifications
Add comprehensive unit and integration test coverage
Consider implementing circuit breaker patterns for external service calls
Add metrics and observability improvements beyond New Relic integration
